blocks.content: Puducherry's demography reflects its composite four-region structure — predominantly Tamil-speaking with distinct Malayalam-speaking (Mahe) and Telugu-speaking (Yanam) minority pockets — alongside a small but historically significant Franco-Indian community.

cells: The large majority of the UT's population resides in the Puducherry region itself, with Karaikal second, and Mahe and Yanam considerably smaller
approx 1,037 females per 1,000 males — notably favourable, among the better sex ratios of any Indian state/UT
Highly urbanised relative to most Indian states, particularly in the Puducherry region itself

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Puducherry's sex ratio (approx 1,037 females per 1,000 males) is notably FAVOURABLE — among the better sex ratios of any Indian state/UT, a frequently tested comparative demographic fact.

items: Tamil is the majority language across most of the UT (Puducherry and Karaikal regions), reflecting the UT's predominantly Tamil Nadu-adjoining geography.

Malayalam is the majority language of Mahe (surrounded by Kerala), and Telugu is the majority language of Yanam (surrounded by Andhra Pradesh) — meaning Puducherry UT is officially and practically multilingual across its four regions, each aligned linguistically with its respective surrounding mainland state.

French retains a limited but symbolically and institutionally significant presence, particularly in Puducherry town, reflecting the region's colonial heritage (Chapter 3) — French-medium schools (including the historic Lycee Francais de Pondichery) and the French Institute of Pondicherry continue to operate, and a small population of Franco-Pondicherrians (Indian-origin French citizens, see Chapter 9) maintains ongoing cultural and administrative ties to France.
English and Hindi are also in use, particularly in administration, education and wider commerce.

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Puducherry UT has FOUR different majority languages across its four regions — Tamil (Puducherry, Karaikal), Malayalam (Mahe), Telugu (Yanam) — each matching the surrounding mainland state's dominant language, a distinctive linguistic-diversity fact directly following from the UT's four-enclave geography (Chapter 1).

A distinctive social feature of Puducherry, dating to the colonial-era citizenship provisions described in Chapter 3, is the continued presence of a small community of Franco-Pondicherrians — Indian-origin residents who hold French citizenship (a right extended to residents of French India under specified historical provisions at the time of the transfer to India) while continuing to live in Puducherry. This community maintains distinctive cultural, linguistic and institutional ties to France, including eligibility to vote in French elections and access to certain French social/educational institutions, a genuinely unusual demographic feature not replicated elsewhere in India.

items: Population (2011): approx 12.47 lakh; sex ratio approx 1,037/1,000 (favourable); literacy approx 86%.
Four different majority languages across the UT's four regions: Tamil (Puducherry, Karaikal), Malayalam (Mahe), Telugu (Yanam).
French retains institutional presence (Lycee Francais de Pondichery, French Institute of Pondicherry); a small Franco-Pondicherrian community holds French citizenship.
